title: How to Compensate CSMs
summary: The different compensation models for customer success teams.
body_text: In their roles helping make customers successful, customer success managers, or CSMs, have a wide range of responsibilities. This can range from complex technical product knowledge to sales and relationship building skills. The needs and requirements of each customer success team can also vary significantly from company to company. Given this wide scope of responsibilities, there are a number of different approaches to compensating CSMs. Determining the best approach for your business requires careful consideration of your business goals as well as the needs of your customers from their success team. There are 3 basic models for compensating CSMs: Base salary: this approach works well when you need CSMs to be neutral resources for your customers Base salary and bonus: the addition of a bonus can help focus CSMs on specific outcomes or metrics Base salary and commissions: commissions make sense for CMSs when they have responsibility and some control over renewals and revenue expansion Our new guide on the types of CSM compensation structures has detailed information on each of these approaches, along with considerations on which might work best for your particular circumstance.

title: Best PEO for Businesses That Want Local Support
summary: Compare local PEO providers with practical criteria for benefits, HR, compliance support, pricing, and local service.
body_text: Best PEO for Businesses That Want Local Support 8:23 Small and mid-sized businesses need more than HR tools. They need HR support that works in the real world, where benefits questions, payroll issues, compliance responsibilities, and employee concerns often overlap. That is why many employers look for a local PEO: a partner that can combine professional employer organization services with practical, relationship-based support. In this guide, we’ll cover: What a local PEO is What strong local support should look like Why local context matters for compliance support How to compare local PEO providers before choosing a partner Start by understanding what “local PEO” actually means. What Is a Local PEO? A local PEO is a professional employer organization that provides HR, payroll, benefits administration, compliance support, and risk management with services in your local market. For many small and mid-sized businesses, the value is not just outsourcing HR tasks . It’s having a practical local team that understands the region where the business operates. A local PEO may support your business through: HR administration: onboarding, employee documentation, handbook support, and manager guidance Payroll support: payroll processing, tax administration support, and related recordkeeping Benefits administration: access to health insurance, medical benefits, open enrollment, deductions, and employee questions Compliance guidance: support around federal, state, and local employment law requirements Risk management: workers’ compensation , safety programs, and claims-related support A strong local PEO should feel less like a vendor and more like an extension of the business, especially when employees need help with coverage, managers need guidance, or owners want a clearer path through HR complexity. What Should Local PEO Support Look Like in Practice? A local PEO should give business owners more than a platform or a menu of outsourced HR services. The real value is practical support when payroll, benefits, compliance, and employee issues overlap in the real world. For example, open enrollment is not just a benefits task. Employees may need help understanding coverage options , managers may need reminders about deadlines, payroll deductions need to be set up correctly, and the business may need documentation to support its compliance responsibilities. A local PEO should help coordinate those details so the employer is not left trying to connect every piece alone. That kind of support can make a meaningful difference for growing businesses. In one BBSI client story, Griswold Home Care franchise owner Beth Copeland described the value this way: “When I send a question, I get an answer, always. That never happened before. We actually know who’s supporting us, and they know our business.” Strong local PEO support should feel: Accessible: the business knows who to contact when questions come up Contextual: advisors understand the employer’s size, industry, workforce, and region Coordinated: payroll, benefits, HR, and risk management teams are not operating in silos Practical: guidance is clear enough for owners and managers to act on Consistent: support does not depend on starting over with a new representative every time When evaluating a local PEO, business owners should look beyond the service list and ask how support actually works day to day. Who answers employee questions? Who guides open enrollment? Who helps managers think through sensitive workforce issues? The answers reveal whether the provider is simply administering tasks or truly supporting the business. Why Does Local Context Matter for Compliance Support? Compliance support is one of the clearest places where local PEO service can matter. Federal requirements create one layer of responsibility, but many day-to-day HR decisions are shaped by state employment law, local rules, industry norms, and the realities of the employer’s workforce. Local context can be especially useful for: State-specific employment law updates Benefits notices and open enrollment communication Leave and accommodation processes Workers’ compensation and safety requirements Multi-location workforce questions The key is clarity. A strong local PEO should help the business understand what requirements may apply, what processes need attention , and when outside legal or tax counsel may be appropriate. How Should You Evaluate the Best Local PEO for Your Business? (Buyer’s Checklist) Businesses often look for a local PEO because they want HR support that feels accessible, practical, and connected to their market. Global scale can be valuable, but many small and mid-sized employers still want a familiar advisor who understands their workforce, region, and day-to-day business challenges. That does not mean a local provider is always better than a global provider. The right question is: Which support model fits the way your business actually operates? Evaluation Area Local Support Model Centralized Support Model Support mode Dedicated local contacts and regional advisors Centralized support teams and standardized processes Employment law guidance More familiarity with state and local requirements Broad national compliance infrastructure Benefits support More accessible help with employee questions and enrollment Larger systems for plan administration and employee self-service Best fit Businesses that want hands-on guidance Businesses that prioritize scale, uniformity, and centralized tools A payroll issue , a benefits enrollment question, a workers’ compensation concern, or a manager’s employment law question usually needs more than a generic answer. It needs context. A provider familiar with the local business environment can help employers think through those situations with more practical nuance. Buyer’s Checklist: Use These Questions to Compare Local PEO Providers: What does “local support” mean in your service model? Ask whether the provider offers local consultants, regional teams, in-person meetings, or a dedicated point of contact. How do you support benefits administration? Look for clear answers around health insurance, medical coverage , open enrollment, employee questions, deductions, and plan communication. What compliance support is included? Ask how the PEO helps businesses stay current with applicable employment law requirements, documentation, notices, and reporting responsibilities. How transparent are your pricing and contract terms? Request a sample invoice, service agreement, and explanation of what is included, optional, or billed separately. Can you provide references from similar businesses? The strongest comparison is often another employer with a similar size, industry, workforce, or growth stage. A good evaluation process should reveal more than what the PEO sells. It should show how the provider communicates, how proactive the team is, and whether their guidance feels practical for your business. The right local PEO should make HR feel more manageable, not more complicated. Choose BBSI as Your Local PEO Partner The best local PEO is not simply the provider closest to your office. It is the partner that understands your business, supports your people, and helps bring HR, payroll, benefits administration, compliance guidance, and risk management into a clearer system. For small and mid-sized employers, that kind of support can make daily workforce decisions feel less fragmented and more manageable. BBSI brings that model to businesses across the country, with 900+ employees nationwide, a 98% client satisfaction rate, and local teams for every client. If you are evaluating local PEO options, start with the partner built to meet you where your business actually operates. Connect with BBSI to discuss your workforce, benefits goals, and support needs. Quick Summary This blog explains how small and mid-sized businesses can evaluate a local PEO based on service model, benefits administration, compliance support, and day-to-day responsiveness. It emphasizes that the best local PEO is not just geographically nearby, but connected to the employer’s market, workforce, and practical HR needs. Local PEO Support FAQs What is a local PEO? A local PEO is a professional employer organization that provides HR, payroll, benefits administration, compliance support, and risk management with services connected to a specific region or market. For many employers, the value is having accessible support from people who understand their business environment. How is a local PEO different from a centralized PEO? A local PEO may offer more relationship-based support, regional knowledge, and hands-on guidance, while a centralized PEO may offer broader systems and standardized processes. The right choice depends on the employer’s workforce, support expectations, budget, and compliance needs. What should businesses look for in a local PEO? Businesses should compare local PEO providers based on support model, benefits administration, compliance guidance, pricing transparency, references, and industry fit. The strongest partner should make HR, payroll, benefits, and risk management easier to manage.

title: Dataverse Plugin for Coding Agents: OpenAI and Codex Marketplace Expansion
summary: We’re excited to announce expansion of the Dataverse plugin across additional coding agent marketplaces, meeting developers where they already work. The plugin is now available for OpenAI and Codex.
body_text: The Dataverse plugin for coding agents brings the full power of Microsoft Dataverse directly into the developer’s coding environment. Instead of switching between browser tabs, documentation, and admin portals, developers can describe what they want in natural language and the plugin handles the rest. It routes each request through the right tool: Dataverse MCP server, Python SDK, PAC CLI, or Dataverse CLI. This allows developers to stay in flow and deliver production-grade results without mastering every tool individually. Built on an open-source skill architecture, the plugin enforces least-privilege security, follows documented authentication patterns, and respects existing Dataverse RBAC, making it safe for real enterprise environments from day one. We’re excited to announce expansion of the Dataverse plugin across additional coding agent marketplaces, meeting developers where they already work. The plugin is now available for OpenAI and Codex . This adds to the existing support for Claude, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot . Regardless of which coding agent a team standardizes on, they get the same Dataverse expertise: intelligent skill routing, enterprise-grade guardrails, and a consistent natural-language experience across surfaces. This expansion matters because it reduces adoption friction for customers and partners. Teams can keep their preferred coding agent while using a common Dataverse interaction model for data operations, schema work, solution lifecycle tasks, and environment administration. The result is faster onboarding, more repeatable delivery patterns, and clearer governance alignment without forcing toolchain consolidation. Installing Dataverse plugin for coding agents in ChatGPT and Codex The Dataverse plugin for coding agents is available in the marketplace in both the OpenAI and Codex experiences. Choose your preferred surface, go to Plugins , and search for Microsoft Dataverse . title: What Are Personal Care Services and When Can They Help at Home?
summary: Learn what personal care services are, when they may help at home, and how non-medical support can promote safety, independence, dignity, and caregiver relief.
body_text: Home is supposed to be where we feel most comfortable, independent, and connected to daily life. It is where routines feel familiar, choices feel personal, and people can remain surrounded by the things and memories that matter most. But when daily tasks become harder to manage safely, staying at home may require extra support. Personal care services can help individuals maintain comfort, dignity, and independence at home by providing assistance with everyday routines, personal needs, and non-medical support. What are Personal Care Services? Personal care services provide hands-on, non-medical support with everyday activities that may become difficult because of age, illness, disability, injury, or changes in mobility or memory. These activities are often called activities of daily living, or ADLs. They include essential tasks such as bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, eating, transferring, and moving safely from one place to another. Depending on the person’s needs and the services available, personal care may also include support with meal preparation, medication reminders, light housekeeping, transportation, errands, companionship, and help maintaining a safe daily routine. The goal is not to take independence away. The goal is to provide the right level of support so a person can continue living at home as safely and comfortably as possible. How Personal Care Differs From Medical Care Personal care services are different from skilled medical care. A personal care aide does not replace a nurse, physician, or therapist. Instead, personal care supports the daily activities that help a person maintain comfort, hygiene, nutrition, mobility, and routine at home. For example, a nurse may manage clinical assessments, medications, treatments, or wound care. A personal care aide may help the person bathe safely, get dressed, prepare a meal, move from a bed to a chair, or remember when it is time to take medication. Both types of care are important, but they serve different needs. When Can Personal Care Services Help? Families often begin looking for personal care services when they notice changes in a loved one’s ability to manage daily life at home. Support may be helpful when someone is: Having difficulty bathing, dressing, or grooming. Skipping meals or struggling with meal preparation. Becoming less steady while walking or transferring. Forgetting parts of their daily routine. Recovering after a hospital stay or illness. Spending more time alone and becoming socially isolated. Having trouble keeping the home environment safe and manageable. Needing reminders for medications or appointments. Relying heavily on one family caregiver. Experiencing changes in memory, strength, or mobility. These changes may happen gradually. A loved one may say they are doing fine, while family members notice that laundry is piling up, food is going uneaten, hygiene has changed, or the person seems less confident moving around the home.Personal care services can help close those gaps before they become larger safety concerns. Relief for Family Caregivers Family caregivers often take on more than they realize. They may help with transportation, meals, bathing, medications, appointments, household tasks, and emotional support, sometimes while also managing jobs, children, or other responsibilities. Over time, that level of responsibility can become overwhelming. Personal care services can provide relief by sharing the daily workload. Even a few hours of support each week can give family caregivers time to rest, work, run errands, or simply step back from the constant pressure of being the only person available. This support can also help preserve family relationships. When a caregiver has help with routine tasks, they may have more energy to spend meaningful time with their loved one as a spouse, adult child, sibling, or friend. Helping Older Adults Maintain Independence Accepting help at home can be difficult for some people. They may worry that needing assistance means losing independence. In reality, the right support can often help a person maintain more independence for longer. Personal care services are built around the individual’s needs, preferences, and routines. Care may be provided for a few hours a week, several days a week, or more frequently depending on the situation. Support can be adjusted over time as needs change. For some people, that may mean help with bathing and light housekeeping. For others, it may mean daily assistance with meals, mobility, and personal care. The best care plans are not one-size-fits-all. They are designed around what the person can do, where support is needed, and how to help them remain as comfortable and independent as possible. As a member of the Addus HomeCare Family of Companies, we work with you to help tailor a plan that fits your or your loved-one’s lifestyle. When to Start the Conversation Families do not need to wait for a major crisis before asking about personal care services. In fact, starting early can help prevent stress, reduce safety concerns, and make the transition to care feel more comfortable. If you are unsure whether personal care is needed, consider these questions: Is my loved one safe while bathing, dressing, and moving around the home? Are meals being prepared and eaten regularly? Is the home environment clean, safe, and manageable? Is one family caregiver becoming overwhelmed? Would regular companionship or supervision improve daily life? Are small challenges becoming more frequent or harder to manage? If the answer to any of these questions is yes, personal care services may be worth exploring. Support That Helps Home Remain Home Personal care services can make a meaningful difference for individuals who want to remain at home but need extra support with daily life. With help from a trained caregiver, everyday routines can become safer, more manageable, and less stressful for everyone involved. Whether the need is assistance with bathing, meals, mobility, companionship, or caregiver relief, personal care can provide practical support while honoring the person’s dignity, preferences, and independence. Home should be a place of comfort. Personal care services help make that possible. Reach out to use for more information on how we can help assist you or a loved one maintain your independence.

title: ‘La Velada del año IV’: El nuevo récord global de Twitch
summary: 'La Velada del Año', el espectáculo de boxeo y entretenimiento del creador de contenido Ibai Llanos, se consolida en su cuarta edición como el evento anual con mayor pico de audiencia en directos de Twitch.
body_text: 'La Velada del Año', el espectáculo de boxeo y entretenimiento del creador de contenido Ibai Llanos, se consolida en su cuarta edición como el evento anual con mayor pico de audiencia en directos de Twitch. El evento tuvo lugar el sábado 13 de julio de 2024 en el estadio Bernabéu de Madrid, con unos 80 mil asistentes presenciales1 y 3,8 millones de peak viewers2 en la transmisión de Ibai en Twitch – superando los 3,4 millones del año anterior3 y estableciendo un récord mundial de audiencia en la plataforma. Un despliege cross-platform Más allá de Twitch, el contenido relacionado con el evento alcanzó un engagement de 20,4 millones de interacciones el mismo día de su celebración, a través de las plataformas sociales Facebook, Instagram, X y TikTok, siendo esta última la que lo encabezó con un 65%. La publicación de TikTok que lideró este engagement fue del anfitrión, Ibai, con un vídeo de la actuación de la cantante puertorriqueña Young Miko, que alcanzó los 6 millones de interacciones. El combate por el engagement Analizando los 10 combatientes con mayor engagement la víspera, durante y tras el evento, la streamer mexicana Alanita fue ganadora en el ring y en la batalla en redes sociales con un total de 5,6 millones de interacciones, le siguieron su compatriota ElMariana y el influencer español Peldanyos con 4,7 y 4,3 millones de interacciones en las redes, respectivamente. Las marcas se suman al entretenimiento Durante el evento, varias marcas contribuyeron activamente al espectáculo y colaboraron en la creación de contenido.
